summary: Steel lookout on Sexton Mountain, Josephine County, Oregon; the 2006 vandal-destroyed tower was replaced in 2007, and it is fenced and unmanned by 2021.

facts.design: Flat-roof cab on a 40-foot steel tower, built 2007; an older D-6 cupola cabin from 1921 still stands on the summit

access.note: Summit road is gated; the tower is fenced and the 2021 visitor found no way to gain access. No reopening found.

visit.trail_note: About 5.3 miles of spur road to a gate, then about 0.8 mile on foot to the summit (2021 visit); the tower is fenced

corrections.proposed: Flat-roof cab on a 40-foot steel tower (2007); the D-6 cupola cabin is the older 1921 cabin still on site
corrections.why: The D-6 cupola cabin is the 1921 structure. The 2007 report proposes moving it to Tillamook, and the register describes the current lookout as a flat-roof cab on a steel tower.
9.1 m is about 30 feet, the height of the 1962/63 wooden tower. The register gives 40 feet for the 2007 steel tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a tent in 1914 and a cupola cab in 1921; a 1919 Grants Pass item already mentions a newly completed station. The story gives the sources' dates and does not pick one.
The register says 1963; the Weebly listing gives construction in 1962 (work begun September 1962). The story says 1962 or 1963.
The register dates the tower to 2007; the Weebly listing says completed October 2007 and in service for the 2008 fire season. The story reports both.
The register says ODF flat cab; the Weebly listing says Amort style lookout cab. Not used in the story.

notes_for_editor: Brief's design 'D-6 cupola cabin' describes the older 1921 cabin, not the current tower; the current lookout is a flat-roof cab on a 40-foot steel tower (NHLR). Brief's height 9.1 m matches the 1962/63 wooden tower, so it is corrected to 12.2 m (40 ft, converted). Build year 2007 is consistent in the register but the Weebly listing says completed October 2007 and in service 2008. Sources disagree on the 1962/63 tower year and the 1914/1919/1921 early dates; the story reports the disagreement. 'Unmanned' and 'fenced' rest on a 2021 blog visit (as_of 2021-07), not a current official source. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the gate and fence. The 1931 Department of Commerce weather-cabin contract is in the Weebly listing but not footnoted in the story. Photos not added.
